problemFit.koeln.intro: Cologne's bicycle network consists of two complementary components:
problemFit.koeln.ringsBody: The conversion of former car lanes on Cologne's Inner Ring into continuous 2.50-meter-wide bicycle lanes with a 30 km/h speed limit. The measure was approved by city officials in 2016 and provisionally completed in December 2024.
problemFit.koeln.routesBody: Eight radial commuter routes from the outer city districts to the city center, as well as a connecting bike ring. The network was developed in collaboration with neighboring municipalities.
problemFit.koeln.goalBody: To create a continuous, safe bicycle network that sustainably increases the share of bicycle traffic in the modal split and reduces private motorized transportation.
The project builds a continuous network of protected bike lanes and expands the Vélib' bike-sharing system across the city, aiming to give more residents (regardless of age, sex, or ability) convenient and affordable access to sustainable transport.
By shifting car trips to bicycles and calming motorized traffic, the project reduces traffic-related air pollution and noise, helping to lower the city's per-capita environmental impact.
problemFit.paris-marne-la-vallee.overvie: Paris's "Plan Vélo" is a flagship project of the city's Climate Action Plan, created to tackle the pollution, congestion, and emissions caused by decades of car-centric planning. Before the plan, a large share of trips depended on private motorized vehicles, pushing up greenhouse-gas emissions, air pollutants, and noise while cycling stayed marginal and often unsafe. Plan Vélo responds by making the bicycle a genuine primary mode of transport rather than a niche one. It works through three combined levers: infrastructure (a continuous network of protected bike lanes, many reclaimed from former car lanes, plus secure bike parking), traffic calming (lower speed limits and restrictions on through-traffic that take road space back from cars), and the expansion of public bike services such as the Vélib' bike-sharing system. Together these measures aim to give residents across the whole city safe, convenient, and affordable access to sustainable mobility. By moving journeys off cars and onto bikes, the project cuts emissions and pollution at the source and now serves as an internationally cited model for sustainable urban mobility.
